items.reason: The cache entry is written before store admission succeeds and remains after rejection, allowing retries to bypass the device limit.
Omitting X-Grafana-Device-Id makes TagDevice return nil, bypassing device-limit enforcement during authentication.
Separate count and upsert operations let concurrent new devices pass the capacity check and exceed the limit.
A rejected device retains its prematurely written cache entry, so a retry authenticates without enforcing the limit.
The non-atomic count-and-insert admission decision allows concurrent requests to consume the same remaining capacity.
Caching before a successful store write lets rejected or in-flight admissions appear successful to subsequent requests.
The count and subsequent upsert lack serialization, allowing concurrent admissions to exceed the configured device limit.
